newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Indonesia allocates 2.3 million barrels July LSWR.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia allocates 2.3 million barrels July LSWR.

text.p: Indonesia's state oil company Pertamina has allocated a total of 2.3 million barrels of low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) for July lifting, industry sources said on Tuesday.
This is significantly lower than its previous allocation of about 3.1 million barrels for lifting in June, they said.
The reduction in volume was caused by the shutdown of some units at its 200,000 barrel-per-day Balikpapan refinery for maintenance from July 10 for 32 days.
Traders said they expected Pertamina to allocate a further 300,000-400,000 barrels later this month.
They said that British Petroleum was allocated 1.1 million barrels, and Pertamina's two affiliates each received 300,000 barrels.
The cut in allocation was expected to boost LSWR prices currently assessed at between $15.70 and $16.00 per barrel, traders said.
They said increased demand from Japan during summer would give prices further support.
Over one million barrels have already been shipped to Japan in June, traders said.
